steps.speaker: Netizen
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>HalfDayFireworks^^:</color> Here's a pic. Pretty mid imo. I'd say a solid 6.

steps.speaker: Netizen
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Ehui&:</color> Ugly as ****. If I looked like that I wouldn't dare to go outside, haha.

steps.speaker: Netizen
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Messia*:</color> Passable for me. That coat tho... Ummm, no comment.

steps.speaker: Netizen
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>GimmeGimme:</color> LOL, no wonder gotthe face covered on TV!
More and more people point their phone cameras at you surreptitiously when passing by you.
<color=#b0e7b4>Gray Mirror Virality ■■■■□</color>

steps.speaker: Provocative Voice
steps.content: "I'm declaring war on Gray Mirror!"
A voice in the crowd does an impression of you, causing the surrounding passersby to snicker.

steps.speaker: Netizen
steps.content: 〇△〇: Guys, if we vote him out now, can we witness the rumored Purge?
steps.female_content: <color=#fb9259>〇△〇:</color> Guys, if we vote her out now, can we witness the rumored purging ceremony?

steps.speaker: Netizen
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Ming·Zi:</color> Genius! Keylan would have come up with the same idea.
<color=#b0e7b4>Gray Mirror Virality ■■■■■</color>

steps.speaker: Netizen
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>BombMan:</color> Apparently a Corruptor will crawl out of the phone?

steps.speaker: Netizen
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>CopperCap:</color> Oh ****, someone lied to me. I thought you get sucked into the phone.

steps.speaker: Netizen
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Vanished_Road_Sign:</color> Boring. Better just drop a bomb. I mean, art is explosion! (I'm not on the Fifth Avenue anyway, lol.)
<color=#b0e7b4>Gray Mirror Virality ■■■■■</color><color=#dc143c>■■■■</color>
The Purge will likely happen again soon. You must quickly get away from the crowd. A passerby taps your shoulder jokingly, but you ignore it.

steps.speaker: Netizen
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>ExchangeSundae:</color> The vote has started already? Wait for me!

steps.speaker: Netizen
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Capass:</color> Wait, if you vote him out, what's left to watch on the live news show? I hadn't seen anything so entertaining in ages.
<color=#b0e7b4>Gray Mirror Virality ■■■■■</color><color=#dc143c>■■■■■■■■■■</color>
The light turns green, and you quickly start moving, but a large crowd is coming toward you. Someone even pushed you. It's almost impossible to break free.
<color=#b0e7b4>Gray Mirror Virality ■■■■■</color><color=#dc143c>■■■■■■■■■■■■■■</color>
<color=#b0e7b4>Gray Mirror Virality ■■■■■</color><color=#dc143c>■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■</color>
<color=#dc143c>Gray Mirror Virality ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■</color>
Watch out!
Clack!
You get hit on the forehead. Amid the crowd's gasps, you can barely make out a hint of low laughter.

steps.speaker: Dazed Voice
steps.content: Haha, serves you right! That clown is completely stunned. What a masterstroke. Keep up with the trial, warrior!
...You thought it was the vote triggered the Purge, and shackles stirred in your palm ready to resist the incoming Mania. But it turns out to be someone has thrown a stone at you.
A figure desperately cuts through the surrounding crowd and comes in front of you.
Back off! You bunch of jerks, get away!!!

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, come with me. You... you're bleeding a lot!
You wipe your forehead, and indeed your hand comes away covered in crimson.

The journalist's expression changes from shock to anger. She turns to charge into the crowd, but you stop her. The shackles have quieted down, and you pull her back, keeping her out of the cameras' view.
Bianca looks bewildered as you take her camera and check the footage. The crowd has calmed down slightly. You look down at the camera and begin to speak.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Nice pose. You sure are good at throwing stuff at people. Assault and provocation... We've got evidence for several charges here. It's all clearly recorded.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You can still apologize before I send this video to the Public Security Bureau. Or would you like to personally learn the consequences of disrupting public services?
You look around and see some shocked faces, likely due to the blood smeared across half your face. Eastsiders probably aren't used to bloody sights like this.
You pretend to reach into your pocket as if you're searching for your gun. The response is a scream a few meters away.

steps.speaker: Frightened Figure
steps.content: Psychopath??!! Move! Get out of my way!!!
${PlayerName}

For the first time, you see the true nature of those who have flocked to witness your trial. Unlike the brutal gangs of West District, they're just ordinary people who have come out of the dark web back to reality, even appearing somewhat frightened.
Of course, you carry no weapon in your pocket, and Bianca's camera didn't capture the moment of the attack. Watching the dispersing crowd, you hand the camera back to Bianca.

options: The Public Security Bureau will handle this. Let's go.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: ...Okay.
[Deserted street, dusk]

steps.speaker: New Post on the Dark Web
steps.content:
"Gray-coated figure seen terrorizing the street! He threatened ordinary citizens with an unlicensed weapon! If not for the heroic resistance of the crowd, the consequences would have been unimaginable!"

"I was there! He smeared the victim's blood on his face to intimidate the crowd! A violent, anti-social lunatic! He's crazy!!"
steps.female_content: ...I've surveyed the entire area. Besides the ventilation ducts in the dome installed by the owner, there's only one way out.

steps.content: Bianca throws her phone down furiously.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: They're twisting the truth! I should have recorded the event! More people will be on your side for sure!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Huh? That'd prove I was fabricating a lie in front of the crowd. I'd be accused of perverting the course of justice if I got exposed. My superiors would not let me off.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Surely they won't care about that. I'll help you cover it up. Let's say you were just trying to protect an innocent journalist there. That'll definitely win you a lot of fans and shut the haters up!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No. Our goal is to turn everyone into my hater. Why are you helping me gain fans? Don't drag more people into this. My colleagues can't keep up with protecting more targets than there already are.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We're on the right track. All the Inferior votes are now directed at me. The more concentrated and intense the Mania fluctuations, the better we can locate the source. And we won't have to worry about ordinary people getting attacked.
The Bianca you know would be applauding and celebrating the surge in votes, but now she just looks down and seems a little dejected.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: I'm starting to regret this... Had I known you'd come under fire like this, I wouldn't have done that news program with you.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: The more I see those ridiculous comments online, the angrier I get... It's too much... Just disgusting!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Hey, cheer up. You don't have to see them anymore. Out of sight, out of mind, right?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: All the cursing is just to vent their anger. It's not like they're shooting me with real bullets. Speaking of which, I happen to know the master of cursing from Syndicate. You won't believe how adorable she is.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: But they've already come out of the internet and hurt you physically! Look at your head!
She pokes at your recently bandaged forehead sulkily.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Even if Mania disappears, those guys will still hide in the crowd, in the shadows. As long as bad deeds go unpunished, they'll dare to do anything! They can always find ways to justify their behavior and even be smug about it!

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Why don't you punish them? Doesn't it anger you to see bad people slip through law and order?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Don't change the subject!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright, I admit I was careless. I was too focused on chasing Mania that I didn't pay much attention to Gray Mirror. Maybe the real guns and bullets have numbed me. This online malice behind the screen doesn't feel real.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But isn't it the same for those people we saw? Look how scared they were of the blood and of getting caught. They seemed to only realize they'd crossed the line when the stone was thrown. When they cast their Inferior votes to eliminate the bad guys on Gray Mirror, they don't realize they're committing murder, nor do they feel liable for their actions.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If I lose my temper and act out, how am I any different from them? ...Well, there is a difference.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: At that moment, I truly held a power strong enough to shred Corruptors. If I were to indulge my impulse and target defenseless ordinary people... I would definitely become a monster who's way more corrupt than those Gray Mirror fanatics you despise.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I can't make headlines under your coverage that way. I still want to be your partner in justice.
Your casual remark eases Bianca a bit. For once, she watches you quietly, as if waiting for you to continue.

options: I believe a trial is a very serious matter.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It requires tireless evidence gathering and investigation, impartial, objective, and comprehensive consideration, professional expertise, the self-awareness that you could be wrong, and the courage to take responsibility. Only then does one have the right to sanction and harm others in the name of justice.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Human emotions and occasional hatred should not degrade into crimes. It is Gray Mirror who's transformed Mania into the gun of justice and handed it to everyone. It's even helped them unlock it and brainwashed them that killing can be justified, absolving them from the guilt...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This app is the real culprit. I need to focus my energy on uncovering the mastermind behind it and destroying Gray Mirror to truly put an end to this.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll rest here for a bit before I set off. As long as there's still a chance to interrupt this evil plan, I'll do whatever I can to seize it.
Bianca remains silent for a while.
She doesn't answer but keeps staring at you. Then, she suddenly pokes your face.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What, is there something on my face?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: No, I'm just happy... I touched the real you!

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: You've cleared my confusion, and I've made a decision. So I'm happy now!
She suddenly jumps up and runs off, leaving you there alone.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Wait, what decision?

From the moment you met Bianca, you've found it hard to keep up with her pace, whether it was the excitement and curiosity about Corruptors at your first meeting or her sudden disappearance now. She seems simple-minded, yet there's always something inexplicably complicated about her.

It's only after she's gone that you realize it's already evening in Eastside. The sunset reflects off the glass curtain walls, creating an ambience starkly different from that of Syndicate. Somehow you feel slightly relieved, perhaps because of the scenery, or maybe your comforting words for Bianca had the same effect on yourself.
You're still a few votes short, but you've recovered enough energy. That isolated and deserted street recommended by the Public Security Bureau is nearby. Time to get to work.
You are about to get up when a blurry figure dashes toward you exuberantly. Then, you feel something ice-cold pressed against your cheek.
[Date CG]

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Here, I bought you an apple juice!

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Thank you for your golden words! Let's celebrate the fact that we're both still alive! Cheers!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So you went to buy juice just now?
She nods, eagerly watching you take the sweating can.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Um, cheers?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Cough, cough, cough, cough!
You choke on the fizz and try your best not to spew out the drink.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Hold on... Cough, say that again, what's this?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Just apple juice! Hehe.
The chill of the fizzy drink fades in your mouth, replaced by a sharp burning sensation.
Seeing her mischievous smile, you know you should have been wary of this "apple juice".

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Have some more. Come on, don't make me drink alone!
She grabs your sleeve and keeps tugging at it.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Please, Ashy, our wicked villain, the Exterminator... Pretty please?
You down the whole can of apple juice without incident, but Bianca herself can barely walk in a straight line now.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Here's to the second day of our acquaintance! Cheers!

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Here's... Here's to getting e-everyone's attention with Gray Mirror... To finding my partner in justice! Cheers!

You carefully keep her from toppling while thinking of a tactful excuse to send her away, fearing that this genius, now drunk on apple juice, might get herself into even more unthinkable trouble soon.

Trusting you to take care of her, she babbles on under the sunset, telling you everything from her journalist qualification exam to the camera she bought with her first salary. Finally, she gets to her most unforgettable experience as a journalist...
That was three months ago when she had her first encounter with Gray Mirror. A hint of confusion and hesitation finally appears on her usually carefree face.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: ...So, I think, I may have, possibly... stumbled upon Gray Mirror's server before.
Where was this server? What did it look like?
Bianca shakes her head groggily.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Just some ordinary machines, but... they were covered in this wriggling black stuff. When they ran at high power, the black goo pulsed and turned into di-different monsters, then slipped back into the machines.
Mania contamination! Your mind immediately clears up at her words.

It's not some sci-fiesque monster transformed into data and traveling at light speed you've imagined. The source of this new Mania crisis is in fact a <color=#fb9259>massive physical server</color> plagued by contamination in the material form.

It must be difficult to transport. If Bianca could find it, it's likely in DisCity. Despite their continuous efforts, your colleagues still haven't been able to locate it... A familiar possibility crosses your mind.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: And then, I got caught. The black goo wrapped around my waist, and two people in black raincoats pinned me down. And I saw these messages on a tiny screen, saying they were developer and the dark web's master. He asked what I was doing and who sent me.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: I fought as hard as I could, using all my instincts as a journalist. I barely made it out. But when I got back, something felt off.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: The injuries on my body and the evidence I had were gone. My memory was blurry, and I couldn't remember much. It felt like a dream. I started thinking it was just my imagination because of my obsessive investigation. And, well, a journalist can't take made-up stories seriously...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll pretend these are just your apple juice drunken ramblings. Tell me everything. I'll investigate it to verify the truth when I get back.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Hehe... Sure, I'll tell you, I'll tell, hic, you everything... Although my memory is all blurry now, I do remember one thing.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: On the squooshy, gloomy faces of those "people", I saw a vertical golden eye.
It's the Underground! They're using sorcery to hide their base and the source of contamination.
At this moment, the mention of your "old friend" confirms your suspicion. You feel relieved as if you've found a shortcut.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Thank you, Bianca. This is very crucial information to us. You've really been a great help.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Whoever is letting Mania and Gray Mirror harm people, I swear to root them out and clean up this mess they've created.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Hey, I heard it, so now you must keep your promise and do it... This way, Bianca's dream can come true...
Bianca turns the juice can upside down and shakes it to ensure not a drop is left, and then reluctantly throws it into the trash can.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Eh? Didn't I tell you? My dream, well, it's, it's... Blurrgh...
At least she has the decency not to vomit on you.
In the end, you watch this "Apple Juice junkie" expertly hail a cab, climb into the back seat, and state her destination. You only breathe a sigh of relief once the cab is out of sight.

You open Gray Mirror again to check your votes. Thanks to the commotion on the Fifth Avenue, attention on the Exterminator has reached a new high. The Bureau's technology department and the supporting police forces have successfully assembled nearby.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Next...
[In the car]

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Ugh... Excuse me, where are we going?

steps.speaker: Driver
steps.content: Didn't you just give me your apartment address?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Did I? My head is spinning, maybe I made a mistake...

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: I changed my mind. Let's go to DisTV.
